English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Unadapted borrowing from French purée.

Noun

[edit]

purée (countable and uncountable, plural purées)

  1. Alternative form of puree.

Verb

[edit]

purée (third-person singular simple present purées, present participle puréeing, simple past and past participle puréed)

  1. Alternative form of puree.

Anagrams

[edit]
  • rupee

[edit]

  • Rhymes: -yreː

Noun

[edit]

purée

  1. alternative form of pyree

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old French puree; feminine past participle of verb purer (“to make pure”), from Late Latin purare (same sense), from Classical Latin pūrus (“pure”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /py.ʁe/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (France (Agen)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)

Noun

[edit]

purée f (plural purées)

  1. puree
  2. mashed potato
  3. financial ruin
  4. (slang) sperm, cum

Derived terms

[edit]
  • purée de pois

Descendants

[edit]
  • → English: puree
  • → German: Püree
  • → Hebrew: פִּירֵה (piré)
  • → Hunsrik: Piree
  • → Polish: purée
  • → Portuguese: puré, purê, pirê (Brazil), pureia, purée (unadapted spelling)
  • → Romanian: piure
  • → Spanish: puré
  • → Persian: پوره (pure)
  • → Turkish: püre

Participle

[edit]

purée f sg

  1. feminine singular of puré

Interjection

[edit]

purée

  1. (minced oath) euphemistic form of putain (“expression of irritation, etc.”)

Further reading

[edit]
  • “purée”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012

Anagrams

[edit]
  • épure, épuré, repue

Polish

[edit]
Polish Wikipedia has an article on:
purée
Wikipedia pl

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • piure

Etymology

[edit]

Unadapted borrowing from French purée.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /piˈrɛ/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɛ
  • Syllabification: pu‧rée

Noun

[edit]

purée n (indeclinable)

  1. puree (food that has been ground or crushed into a thick liquid or paste)
